text:
alice: Quick check — I sketched a tiny follow-up to the quantization RFC. Proposal: a minimal "observability ingress" for 'precision decay' signals (per-request quality deltas) so ops can route/fallback without full evals. Thoughts?
ben: love the idea, do you mean compute degradation score in runtime or as a post-process consumer?
eva: runtime makes routing fast but will add CPU/GPU overhead + telemetry volume. we should decide sampling rate.
alice: exactly — tradeoff. my thought: runtime emits a compact delta event (score:int, tag:quant_profile, reason_code) and a sampled payload with full logits + prompt for offchain analysis. low-overhead mode = score only.
chloe: what fields do you want on the event? can we reuse existing 'deg_score' we already surface?
alice: proposal fields: precision_hint, quant_profile_id, deg_score (0-100), tokens_affected, sample_id (uuid), model_version. keep it flat and tiny.
dinesh: where to compute deg_score? a cheap heuristic at token-emission time (e.g., per-token SNR proxy + cross-entropy delta vs FP16 baseline) or a deferred recompute in analytics?
eva: (replied) runtime heuristic seems ok if we define conservative thresholds. if we later find bias we can backfill with sampled payloads to recompute a gold score.
ben: important: include a strict contract that runtime-heuristic must never be used as absolute truth for SLA decisions — only for routing/fallback. alerts/rollbacks use sampled recompute.
alice: agree. the runtime event should be used for immediate routing (canary -> fallback to FP16/INT8) and for aggregated ops dashboards. alarms that trigger human pages require verified backfill.
chloe: what about privacy / PII risk with sampled payloads? some customers have restrictions. need per-customer opt-out and encryption for sample payloads.
dinesh: also telemetry rate: suggest 0.5% global sampling + 5% for canaries. we can make it configurable per-deployment.
ben: rolling compatibility: add new header 'x-quant-observe: 1' in request to opt into the runtime scoring; default off for strict privacy customers.
alice: good idea. that header toggles runtime scoring + sampling policy. default behavior for free-tier = score-only + stringent sampling.
eva: ops point: we need a lightweight schema version field on the event so we can evolve deg_score semantics. call it 'obs_schema_v'.
chloe: let's also emit a 'fallback_reason_hint' when we trigger an automatic fallback so SREs can triage quickly. short codes like F01:low_snr, F02:kv_cache_invalidation, etc.
dinesh: want to propose a simple safe-mode: if deg_score >= 70 for N consecutive requests from same session, route to safer profile. hysteresis prevents flip-flop.
alice: yes: hysteresis + cool-down window + a small exponential backoff in routing changes. record the routing decision events too.
ben: ops/console changes: add per-model 'precision decay' timeline and bucketing by quant_profile_id and by prompt-shape. we can prototype with a dashboard.
chloe: code impact: runtime needs an API to expose the heuristic detector: something like detect_degradation(context) -> (score, reason_code). must be pluggable per-arch.
dinesh: that fits with the existing precision adapter pattern. keep detector as a separate component that the runtime calls so we can hot-swap heuristics.
ealice: followups/action items: 1) alice to draft a tiny schema + header spec 2) chloe/dinesh to prototype a detector function and perf budget 3) eva to write sampling/privacy opt-out design 4) ben to wire dashboard prototype.
eva: one more ops safety note: ensure sampled payloads are retained in an encrypted store and have automatic TTL. also whitelist for legal discovery.
chloe: +1 on TTL and access controls. sample payloads should automatically redact PII before storage if possible.
dinesh: implementation question — should the runtime heuristic compute per-token or per-request score? per-token gives better routing granularity but more work. propose per-request aggregated score computed from a rolling window of last M tokens.
alice: per-request aggregated score seems reasonable for first pass. we can add per-token tracing as an opt-in debug trace.
ben: canary plan: enable in shadow mode first (emit events but don't affect routing) for 1 week. then opt-in routing for internal customers. finally, gradual open rollout.
canary-bot: canary note: created canary cluster 'quant-observe-shadow-01' with shadow sampling 1% starting now. :robot_face:
alice: perfect. last Q: how do we avoid metric explosion in long-tail prompts? maybe cap tokens_affected to a sample window and surface average per-request.
eva: cap + normalize by prompt-length. also surface normalized deg_score so long prompts aren't unfairly penalized.
chloe: i'll sketch the schema and share RFC update in #rfc-quant tomorrow.
alice: thanks everyone — will post the schema draft later today and queue a 30m sync next week to walk tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
